BACKGROUND

(A) The Client plans to enter the United Kingdom market. It wishes to obtain market research, data collection, business analysis and advisory services to inform its plans.

(B) The Provider carries on business as a provider of market research and commercial advisory services.

(C) The parties wish to record the terms on which the Provider will provide services to the Client under one or more statements of work. The first is Statement of Work No. 1.

AGREED TERMS

1. Definitions and Interpretation

1.1 In this Agreement the following definitions apply:

1.2 In this Agreement:

(a) clause, schedule and annex headings do not affect interpretation;

(b) a reference to a statute or statutory provision is to it as amended, extended or re-enacted from time to time;

(c) "writing" or "written" includes email;

(d) "including" and similar words are illustrative only and do not limit the generality of the words before them; and

(e) a reference to a party includes its successors and permitted assigns.

2. Structure of this Agreement and Order of Precedence

2.1 This Agreement sets out the general terms on which the Provider will provide Services to the Client. Each SOW forms a separate contract that incorporates these terms.

2.2 A SOW is binding only when both parties have signed it. The Provider has no obligation to provide any services except under a signed SOW.

2.3 If there is any conflict or inconsistency between the documents forming the Agreement, they take precedence in this descending order:

(a) the clauses of this Agreement;

(b) the relevant SOW, excluding its annexes;

(c) the Payment Schedule;

(d) the Approved Research Plan; and

(e) any other document referred to in the SOW, including the forms in Annex 2.

2.4 A SOW may vary a specific clause of this Agreement for that SOW only. It does so only if it expressly identifies the clause being varied and states that the variation is intended to take precedence.

3. Commencement and Duration

3.1 This Agreement takes effect on the date on which both parties have signed it (the "Effective Date"). It continues until terminated under clause 18.

3.2 Each SOW takes effect on the date on which both parties have signed it. It continues until the Services under it have been completed and all Charges under it have been paid, unless terminated earlier under clause 18.

4. Provider's Obligations

4.1 The Provider shall perform the Services:

(a) in accordance with this Agreement, the relevant SOW and, once approved under clause 7.8, the Approved Research Plan;

(b) with reasonable skill and care and in accordance with Good Industry Practice; and

(c) in accordance with applicable law.

4.2 The Provider shall use reasonable endeavours to meet the timetable in the relevant SOW. All dates are estimates unless the SOW expressly states otherwise. Time is not of the essence for performance of the Services.

4.3 The Provider shall appoint a project lead to act as the Client's principal point of contact for the Services.

4.4 The Provider may replace any of its personnel engaged in the Services with personnel of suitable skill and experience. If it replaces a key person named in the SOW, it shall notify the Client.

4.5 Where the Provider's personnel attend the Client's premises or use the Client's systems, the Provider shall comply with the Client's reasonable security and site policies. This applies only to policies notified to the Provider in writing in advance.

5. Client's Obligations and Client Delay

5.1 The Client shall:

(a) co-operate with the Provider in all matters relating to the Services;

(b) provide the Client Materials, information, access and decisions reasonably required by the Provider, in a timely manner and in any event in accordance with the Client Dependencies;

(c) appoint a project contact with authority to make decisions on its behalf in relation to the Services, and notify the Provider of any change;

(d) respond to the Provider's reasonable requests for information or decisions within [NEGOTIABLE: 2] Business Days;

(e) give any Comments on Interim Deliverables, and review Final Deliverables, in accordance with clause 7;

(f) ensure that its nominated attendees are available for briefings, interviews and the D4 Presentation as reasonably scheduled; and

(g) obtain any internal approvals needed for the Services to proceed.

5.2 The Client is responsible for the accuracy and completeness of the Client Materials. The Client warrants that it has all rights needed to provide the Client Materials to the Provider for use in the Services.

5.3 "Client Default" means any failure or delay by the Client, or by its personnel, agents or advisers, in performing any of the Client Dependencies or other obligations under this Agreement. It also includes any inaccuracy or incompleteness in the Client Materials.

5.4 If a Client Default prevents or delays the Provider's performance:

(a) the Provider is not liable for any resulting failure or delay;

(b) the timetable is extended by at least the period of delay caused, plus any further period reasonably needed to remobilise; and

(c) the Provider may charge, at the Day Rate, for additional time reasonably incurred as a result. Before doing so, it shall notify the Client in writing of the additional time and the reason for it.

5.5 If one or more Client Defaults delay the Services under a SOW by more than [NEGOTIABLE: 10] Business Days in aggregate, the Provider may, by written notice to the Client, do either or both of the following:

(a) charge reasonable remobilisation time at the Day Rate, as stated in the notice; and

(b) treat the outstanding Services under that SOW as complete for payment purposes. The date of the notice is then the Payment Trigger for all unpaid Fees under that SOW.

5.6 If the Provider gives notice under clause 5.5(b):

(a) the Provider shall complete the outstanding Services within a reasonable time after the Client remedies the Client Default, subject to the availability of suitable personnel; but

(b) if the Client has not remedied the Client Default within [NEGOTIABLE: 60] days after the date of the notice, the Provider's obligation to perform the outstanding Services under that SOW ends. No refund of Fees is then due.

6. Research Plan and Scope

6.1 Under each SOW that includes an initial research plan, the Provider shall prepare and deliver a draft research plan as an Interim Deliverable (Deliverable D1 under SOW No. 1). The draft will set out the research objectives, research questions, scope, methodology, sources, any primary research design and an updated timetable.

6.2 Subject to clause 2.3, once approved under clause 7.8, the Approved Research Plan:

(a) supplements and refines the description of the Services and Deliverables in the SOW;

(b) is the plan against which the Provider prepares the remaining Interim Deliverables; and

(c) is the baseline against which the Final Deliverables are assessed under clause 7.10.

6.3 Any change requested by the Client, after approval, to the scope, methodology, sample, sources or timetable in the Approved Research Plan is a Change. It is subject to clause 8.

6.4 Pending approval of the Approved Research Plan, the Provider may begin desk research on the basis of the draft research plan. Work reasonably performed on that basis forms part of the Services. If the Client later requests a different approach, that work will not be repeated without a Change.

7. Interim Deliverables, Final Deliverables and Acceptance

Classification and delivery

7.1 Each SOW classifies each Deliverable as either an Interim Deliverable or a Final Deliverable. For SOW No. 1:

(a) the Interim Deliverables are D1 (Initial research plan) and D2 (Market and competitor analysis report);

(b) the Final Deliverables are D3 (Final research report) and the D4 Materials; and

(c) the D4 Presentation is a service. It is neither an Interim Deliverable nor a Final Deliverable and is governed by clause 7.17.

[NEGOTIABLE: The classification of D1 and D2 as Interim Deliverables.]

7.2 The Provider shall deliver each Deliverable by email to the Client's project email address in the relevant SOW, or by other agreed means. Each delivery shall be accompanied by:

(a) for an Interim Deliverable, a Comment Form with Part A1 completed; and

(b) for a Final Deliverable, an Acceptance Form with Part B1 completed.

The "Delivery Date" is the day on which the Deliverable is sent, if sent before 5.00 pm on a Business Day. Otherwise it is the next Business Day.

Interim Deliverables: comment process

7.3 The Client may give written Comments on an Interim Deliverable within [NEGOTIABLE: 5] Business Days after its Delivery Date (the "Comment Period"), using Part A2 of the Comment Form or otherwise in writing.

7.4 In relation to Interim Deliverables:

(a) they are not subject to Acceptance or rejection, and no Fees depend on them;

(b) if the Provider receives no Comments within the Comment Period, the Client is treated as having no Comments;

(c) Comments do not suspend the Services; and

(d) Comments are not notices under clause 23. They may be sent to the Provider's project email address.

7.5 The Provider shall consider in good faith all Comments received within the Comment Period. It shall respond to them as follows:

(a) D1. If Comments on D1 are received, the Provider shall issue a revised version of D1 (the "Finalised Research Plan") within [NEGOTIABLE: 3] Business Days after the end of the Comment Period. With it, the Provider shall give a short written response, using Part A3 of the Comment Form, stating for each Comment whether it:

  • has been adopted;
  • has not been adopted, with a brief reason; or
  • is to be treated as a Change request under clause 8.

(b) Other Interim Deliverables. The Provider shall reflect any Comments it adopts in the relevant Final Deliverables. It is not required to reissue the Interim Deliverable unless the SOW provides otherwise. On request, it shall give a short written response in the same form as clause 7.5(a).

7.6 The Provider is not required to adopt any Comment that:

(a) falls outside the scope of the SOW, or, for Interim Deliverables other than D1, outside the Approved Research Plan. Any such Comment may be dealt with as a Change request under clause 8;

(b) disagrees with findings, conclusions, estimates, opinions or recommendations reached by the Provider in the exercise of its professional judgement;

(c) asks the Provider to present findings in a way that, in its reasonable professional judgement, would be misleading or not supported by the evidence; or

(d) the Provider receives after the end of the Comment Period.

7.7 The Provider may take a late Comment into account where it reasonably can. Any rework that the late Comment requires is a Change.

7.8 Approved Research Plan. The Approved Research Plan is the version of D1 approved on the earliest of:

(a) the date on which the Client confirms in writing its approval of the draft D1 or the Finalised Research Plan, including by signing Part A4 of the Comment Form;

(b) if the Provider receives no Comments on D1 within the Comment Period, the end of the Comment Period, in which case the draft D1 is the Approved Research Plan; and

(c) if Comments were received, the date falling [NEGOTIABLE: 2] Business Days after the Finalised Research Plan is issued. However, if within that period the Client notifies the Provider in writing that the Finalised Research Plan does not reflect a Comment that the Provider's response stated had been adopted, the Provider shall correct that omission and reissue the Finalised Research Plan. The reissued plan is approved on the date it is reissued.

[LAWYER REVIEW: Confirm that approval of the scope baseline by deemed approval under clause 7.8(b) and (c) is sufficiently certain to bind the Client.]

Final Deliverables: formal acceptance

7.9 The Client shall review each Final Deliverable within [NEGOTIABLE: 5] Business Days after its Delivery Date (the "Review Period").

7.10 A Final Deliverable meets its Acceptance Criteria if it conforms in all material respects with:

(a) its description in the relevant SOW; and

(b) the Approved Research Plan.

7.11 The Client may not reject a Final Deliverable on the ground that:

(a) it disagrees with any findings, conclusions, estimates, opinions or recommendations reached by the Provider in the exercise of its professional judgement;

(b) the findings are commercially unwelcome or do not support a course of action the Client prefers;

(c) the Final Deliverable reflects limitations in the available data that are disclosed in it;

(d) the alleged defect results from a Client Default, or from inaccuracy or incompleteness in the Client Materials;

(e) the Client's requirements have changed since the Approved Research Plan was approved;

(f) the Final Deliverable does not reflect a Comment that the Provider was not required to adopt under clause 7.6; or

(g) the Final Deliverable contains minor errors, such as typographical or formatting errors, that do not materially affect its use for the Permitted Purpose. The Provider shall correct any such minor errors notified to it within a reasonable time. The correction does not affect Acceptance.

7.12 Rejection notice. To reject a Final Deliverable, the Client must deliver a rejection notice that complies with all of the following:

(a) it must be received by the Provider before the end of the Review Period;

(b) it must be made using Parts B2 and B3 of the Acceptance Form, or another written notice containing the same information;

(c) it must identify each Non-Conformity in reasonable detail, with reference to the relevant Acceptance Criteria; and

(d) it must be sent by email to the Provider's project email address, with a copy to the Provider's notice email address under clause 23.4.

A rejection notice is effective only to the extent it relates to a Non-Conformity. Clause 23.2(d) applies to determine when it is received.

7.13 Invalid rejection notice. If the Provider considers that a rejection notice does not comply with clause 7.12, or relies only on grounds excluded by clause 7.11, it shall notify the Client within [NEGOTIABLE: 2] Business Days after receiving it, giving brief reasons. The Final Deliverable is then Accepted at the later of:

(a) the end of the Review Period; and

(b) [NEGOTIABLE: 2] Business Days after the Provider's notification.

This does not apply if, within that time, the Client delivers a rejection notice that complies with clause 7.12. Either party may refer a disagreement under this clause to clause 24.

7.14 Correction and redelivery. If the Client validly rejects a Final Deliverable, the Provider shall correct the notified Non-Conformities and redeliver it within [NEGOTIABLE: 5] Business Days, or any longer period that is reasonable given the nature of the correction. One round of revisions for each Final Deliverable is included in the Fees.

7.15 Re-review and further rejection. The Client shall review a redelivered Final Deliverable within a further Review Period. That review is limited to whether the previously notified Non-Conformities have been corrected. If the Client gives a further rejection notice that complies with clause 7.12, the parties' project leads shall meet promptly to resolve the matter, and either party may refer it to clause 24. Any further revisions requested by the Client are a Change, except revisions to correct previously notified Non-Conformities.

7.16 Acceptance. A Final Deliverable is Accepted on the earliest of:

(a) the date on which the Client confirms acceptance in writing, including by signing the Acceptance Form;

(b) the end of the Review Period, if the Provider has not received by then a rejection notice that complies with clause 7.12, subject to clause 7.13; and

(c) the date on which the Client uses the Final Deliverable, or any part of it, in its business, or discloses it to any third party other than for the purpose of reviewing it.

D4 Presentation

7.17 Where a SOW includes a presentation (under SOW No. 1, the D4 Presentation):

(a) the presentation is a service and is not subject to Comments or Acceptance;

(b) it is treated as delivered on the date it is given;

(c) once the D4 Materials have been delivered, the Provider shall offer the Client at least [NEGOTIABLE: 3] Business Days on which it is available to give the presentation, each falling on or before the Long-Stop Date;

(d) a "Provider Presentation Failure" occurs if the Provider:

  • fails to offer dates as required by clause 7.17(c); or
  • fails to attend a date agreed with the Client;

(e) if the presentation has not been given by the Long-Stop Date and there has been no Provider Presentation Failure, it is treated as delivered on the Long-Stop Date for payment purposes;

(f) in the case described in clause 7.17(e), the Provider shall still give the presentation on a mutually agreed date within [NEGOTIABLE: 30] days after the Long-Stop Date. After that period, the Provider's obligation to give the presentation lapses; and

(g) if there has been a Provider Presentation Failure, clause 7.17(e) does not apply. The presentation is delivered when it is given on a date the parties agree.

[LAWYER REVIEW: Confirm that the deemed-delivery mechanism in clause 7.17(e) is certain and enforceable.]

General

7.18 Rejection of one Final Deliverable does not delay the Review Period for, or Acceptance of, any other Deliverable, except one that depends directly on the rejected Deliverable.

8. Change Control

8.1 Either party may request a Change by written notice to the other.

8.2 Within [NEGOTIABLE: 5] Business Days after receiving or making a Change request, the Provider shall prepare a draft Change Note. The draft will describe:

(a) the Change;

(b) its effect on the Services, Deliverables and timetable;

(c) any additional Fees, calculated at the Day Rate or set out as a fixed quotation; and

(d) the Payment Trigger for those additional Fees.

8.3 No Change is binding until both parties have signed a Change Note. The Provider is not obliged to perform any Change until then. Signature by an exchange of emails between each party's project contact is sufficient.

8.4 The Provider may make changes to the Services without a Change Note if they are necessary to comply with applicable law, or if they do not materially affect the nature, scope or Fees of the Services. It shall notify the Client of any such change.

8.5 Additional work required because of a Client Default is charged under clause 5.4. It does not need the Client's agreement to a Change Note.

9. Fees, Invoicing and Payment

9.1 The Client shall pay the Fees in accordance with the relevant SOW and its Payment Schedule. Under SOW No. 1, the Fees are a fixed fee of £12,000, exclusive of VAT where applicable. They are payable in two instalments of £6,000, as set out in the Payment Schedule.

9.2 The fixed fee covers only the Services and Deliverables described in the SOW and the Approved Research Plan. It does not include:

(a) Expenses;

(b) Changes; or

(c) additional time charged under clause 5.4 or 5.5.

9.3 Payment Trigger, Invoice Date and Due Date. Each Charge becomes payable in three separate stages.

(a) Payment Trigger. The "Payment Trigger" for a Charge is the event or date on which the Provider becomes entitled to invoice it. Payment Triggers are specified in the Payment Schedule, a Change Note, or clauses 5.5(b) and 19. The Provider shall not issue an invoice for a Charge before its Payment Trigger has occurred.

(b) Invoice Date. The "Invoice Date" is the date shown on the invoice. It must be on or after the Payment Trigger. If an invoice is issued before its Payment Trigger has occurred, its Invoice Date is treated as the date on which the Payment Trigger occurs. The Provider shall use reasonable endeavours to issue each invoice within [NEGOTIABLE: 5] Business Days after the Payment Trigger. A later invoice remains valid, and its Due Date runs from its actual Invoice Date.

(c) Due Date. The "Due Date" of an invoice is the date falling [NEGOTIABLE: 14] days after its Invoice Date. If that date is not a Business Day, the Due Date is the immediately preceding Business Day. The Client shall pay each invoice by its Due Date.

(d) Sending invoices. The Provider shall send invoices by email to the Client's invoicing contact in the relevant SOW. If an invoice is sent more than [NEGOTIABLE: 2] Business Days after its Invoice Date, its Due Date runs from the date on which it is sent instead of its Invoice Date.

(e) Invoice content. Each invoice shall state:

  • the SOW reference;
  • the Payment Trigger relied on;
  • the amount, and VAT where applicable;
  • any purchase order number provided under clause 9.4; and
  • the Provider's bank details.

(f) Method of payment. Payment shall be made in pounds sterling, in cleared funds, to the bank account specified in the invoice. A payment is made when the Provider receives cleared funds.

9.4 If the Client requires a purchase order number to appear on invoices, it shall provide that number before the Start Date. The absence of a purchase order number does not delay any Payment Trigger, Invoice Date or Due Date.

9.5 The Provider is not obliged to begin the Services under a SOW until it has received the first instalment of the Fees in cleared funds. The "Start Date" is the later of:

(a) the target start date specified in the SOW; and

(b) the date on which the Provider receives the first instalment in cleared funds.

All timetable periods in the SOW run from the Start Date.

9.6 All Charges are exclusive of VAT. Where VAT is chargeable on any supply under this Agreement, the Client shall pay it in addition to the Charges, at the applicable rate, on receipt of a valid VAT invoice. # Issue Why it matters for the Provider
A1 "Final delivery" is undefined. It could mean delivery of D3, D4 or both, and it could mean delivery or acceptance. £6,000 (50% of the fee) depends on this wording. An acceptance trigger without deemed acceptance lets the Client hold payment indefinitely.
A2 "Linked to signing" doesn't say when payment falls due, or whether work starts before it is paid. The Provider could work for weeks unpaid.
A3 D4 "presentation" could be a document or a live session. If it is a live session, Client scheduling could delay the second payment trigger. A long-stop date is needed.
A4 The fixed fee sits against an approximate timeframe. Nothing covers Client-caused delay. Without a delay mechanism, the Provider absorbs overruns caused by late Client inputs or feedback.
A5 The Client's place of establishment is unknown. "Planned entry into the UK market" suggests it may be an overseas business, despite the "Ltd" name. This affects the VAT position (UK VAT may not apply to an overseas business customer), enforcement against the Client, credit risk and possibly the currency.
A6 "Data collection" is undefined. It could be desk research, interviews, surveys or a third-party panel. This decides the UK GDPR roles, the subcontractor terms and whether third-party costs fall inside the fixed fee.
A7 "Market-entry advice" and "advisory services" have no boundary. The Client could treat the advice as legal, tax, regulatory or financial advice, or as a guarantee of commercial results. Clear exclusions are needed.
A8 D1 (research plan) has no stated function. If the agreed D1 fixes the scope of D2 and D3, it gives strong protection against scope creep. Otherwise it is just another report.
A9 Payment terms will appear in three documents: the agreement, the SOW and the Payment Schedule. An order-of-precedence clause is needed to avoid inconsistency. I'll include one.
A10 Your instructions don't conflict, but there is a tension. Tying payment to "final delivery" is reasonable for the Client. The Provider is protected only if the acceptance test is objective and has a deemed-acceptance backstop. This is addressed in B3 and B5.

Part B: Essential questions

B1. Where is the Client established?

  • (a) UK-incorporated company. Trade-off: simplest position; standard UK VAT and enforcement.
  • (b) Overseas entity, or UK subsidiary of an overseas group. Trade-off: VAT treatment changes, and you may want a parent guarantee or stricter upfront payment.
  • (c) Not yet known: draft a neutral VAT clause and flag it for lawyer review. (Recommended if unconfirmed) Trade-off: keeps drafting moving but must be resolved before signing.

B2. How should the documents be structured?

  • (a) A standalone project agreement with the SOW and Payment Schedule as schedules. Trade-off: shortest; no reuse for follow-on work.
  • (b) A master Consulting Services Agreement with this SOW as SOW No. 1, and the Payment Schedule and Acceptance Form attached to it. (Recommended) Trade-off: slightly longer, but follow-on UK-entry work only needs a new SOW.

B3. What triggers the second £6,000 instalment?

  • (a) Delivery of D3 and D4. Trade-off: fastest cash for the Provider; the Client may resist.
  • (b) Acceptance of D3 and D4, with deemed acceptance at the end of the review period. A long-stop also applies: payment falls due [X] business days after D3 is delivered if the Client delays the D4 presentation. (Recommended) Trade-off: commercially reasonable while protecting cash flow.
  • (c) Acceptance only, with no deemed acceptance. Trade-off: the Client controls payment timing and can hold it indefinitely.

B4. When is the first £6,000 instalment due?

  • (a) Invoiced on signing and payable before work starts; the timetable runs from receipt of payment. (Recommended) Trade-off: no unpaid work; may delay the start by a few days.
  • (b) Invoiced on signing, payable within [14] days, with work starting immediately. Trade-off: faster start; up to two weeks' work is at risk.

B5. How should acceptance work?

  • (a) A review period of [5] business days and [1] round of revisions. Deliverables may be rejected only for material non-conformity with the SOW description, not for disagreement with findings or conclusions. Deemed acceptance applies. (Recommended) Trade-off: firm and objective; still credible to the Client.
  • (b) A review period of [10] business days and [2] rounds of revisions, on the same objective test. Trade-off: a useful concession to keep in reserve; slows the timetable.
  • (c) No formal acceptance; delivery is enough. Trade-off: most Provider-friendly, but the Client is unlikely to accept it, and the Acceptance Form becomes redundant.

B6. What role should D1 play?

  • (a) Once accepted, D1 fixes the research scope, methods and sample for D2 and D3. Later changes go through change control. (Recommended) Trade-off: strong protection against scope creep; needs prompt Client sign-off.
  • (b) D1 is informational only, and scope is defined solely by the SOW. Trade-off: simpler, but scope stays more open to argument.

B7. What data collection will the Provider actually carry out?

  • (a) Desk research only, using public and licensed sources. Trade-off: minimal data protection exposure.
  • (b) Desk research plus interviews or surveys run by the Provider. Trade-off: the Provider will likely be controller of the respondents' personal data, so notices and consents are needed.
  • (c) As (b), plus a third-party fieldwork agency or panel. Trade-off: subcontractor and data terms are needed, and panel costs must sit inside or outside the fee (see C3).
  • (Recommended: tell me which applies. If you're unsure, I'll draft for (b), the safer and broader position.)

B8. Will the Provider receive personal data from the Client, such as customer lists or contacts to interview?

  • (a) No. The Provider acts as independent controller of its own research data, and deliverables contain only aggregated or anonymised data. (Recommended) Trade-off: cleanest position; no Article 28 processor terms needed.
  • (b) Yes. Trade-off: the Provider acts as processor for that data, so a data processing schedule is needed and the agreement gets longer.

B9. How should IP in the deliverables be allocated?

  • (a) The Client owns the final deliverables once it has paid in full. The Provider keeps its background IP, methods, templates, tools, raw data and know-how, and the Client gets a licence to any of these embedded in deliverables. (Recommended) Trade-off: what the Client expects, while protecting reusable assets; the payment condition gives leverage.
  • (b) The Provider keeps all IP and grants the Client a perpetual, non-exclusive licence for internal business use. Trade-off: the most protective option; likely to be negotiated down.
  • (c) The Client owns everything, including raw data and working papers. Trade-off: gives away assets the Provider could reuse; not advised.

B10. What should the liability cap be?

  • (a) 100% of the fees paid and payable (£12,000), excluding indirect and consequential loss and loss of profit. It would also exclude loss arising from the Client's business or market-entry decisions. (Recommended) Trade-off: market-standard for a fixed-fee advisory project.
  • (b) A higher cap, such as 150–200% of the fees or a fixed sum of £[X]. Trade-off: a concession to keep in reserve; should not exceed your insurance cover.
  • Also: does the Provider hold professional indemnity insurance, and at what level? Your answer will be confirmed and checked against the cap; it is not assumed.

B11. How should the Provider's advice be limited and shared?

  • (a) The advice is market research and commercial analysis only. It is not legal, tax, regulatory, financial or investment advice, and it does not guarantee market-entry outcomes. Deliverables are for the Client's internal use. The Client may share them with its group and professional advisers, but on a non-reliance basis. (Recommended) Trade-off: contains the Provider's exposure; normal for research work.
  • (b) As (a), but named third parties such as investors or lenders may rely on the deliverables if they sign a reliance letter. Trade-off: widens exposure; consider a higher fee.
  • (c) Unrestricted sharing. Trade-off: creates exposure to unknown third parties.

B12. What termination and cancellation rights should apply?

  • (a) The Client may terminate for convenience on [5] business days' notice. The first instalment is non-refundable. Work done in excess of £6,000 is charged at the day rate, capped at the total fee. (Recommended) Trade-off: fair, and protects mobilisation costs.
  • (b) No termination for convenience. Trade-off: strongest for the Provider, but unusual for a six-week project and likely to be refused.
  • (c) Termination for convenience with a refund of the unearned portion. Trade-off: Client-friendly; the Provider risks losing committed time.

B13. How should timetable and delay be handled?

  • (a) Fixed calendar dates for each deliverable. Trade-off: certain, but rigid if the Client is late.
  • (b) An indicative timetable running from the start date. Dates move with Client delay. If Client-caused delay exceeds [10] business days, the Provider may charge for remobilisation or treat the outstanding work as complete for payment purposes. (Recommended) Trade-off: protects the fixed fee against overruns.
  • (c) "Approximately six weeks" with no further mechanism. Trade-off: vague; delay disputes become likely.
